title: EXISTS and correlated subqueries
summary: Subqueries that look at the current row, and the yes/no question EXISTS asks.

steps.title: Correlated subqueries
body: A **correlated** subquery refers to the outer query's current row. Conceptually it runs once **per outer row**:
WHERE x.team = e.team);    -- e is the outer row
*"Earns more than the average of **their own** team."* Each employee gets compared with a different average.
Modern databases often rewrite these into joins internally, but on big tables a correlated subquery in SELECT can still mean millions of tiny queries. Check the plan (module 8).

code: AND e.salary > (SELECT AVG(x.salary) FROM employees AS x WHERE x.team = e.team);
setup: PRAGMA foreign_keys = ON;
CREATE TABLE employees (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, name TEXT, title TEXT, team TEXT, manager_id INTEGER REFERENCES employees(id), salary INTEGER);

steps.title: EXISTS
body: `EXISTS (subquery)` is true when the subquery returns **at least one row**. What it selects doesn't matter, so people write `SELECT 1`:
-- managers: employees that someone reports to
WHERE EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM employees AS r WHERE r.manager_id = m.id);
- `EXISTS` can stop at the first match, so it's usually fast.
- Like `IN`, it never duplicates outer rows.

steps.title: Who manages someone?
prompt: Return the **name** and **title** of every employee who has **at least one direct report**. Use EXISTS.
Tables: `employees(id, name, title, team, manager_id, salary)`; `manager_id` points at another employee (NULL for the CEO).
solution: WHERE EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM employees AS r WHERE r.manager_id = m.id);
setup: PRAGMA foreign_keys = ON;

steps.title: Players who never paid
prompt: Return the **handle** of every player with **no purchases**. Use NOT EXISTS.
Tables: `players(id, handle, country, joined)` and `purchases(id, player_id, item, gems, day)`.
solution: WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM purchases AS x WHERE x.player_id = p.id);
setup: PRAGMA foreign_keys = ON;
CREATE TABLE players (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, handle TEXT, country TEXT, joined TEXT);
CREATE TABLE purchases (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, player_id INTEGER REFERENCES players(id), item TEXT, gems INTEGER, day TEXT);
hints: `WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM purchases AS x WHERE x.player_id = p.id)`

code: (SELECT MAX(x.day) FROM purchases AS x WHERE x.player_id = p.id) AS last_buy
options: Each player's handle with their most recent purchase day (NULL if none)
An error: subqueries can't go in SELECT
The latest purchase day, repeated for every player
steps.explain: A correlated scalar subquery runs per player. For zephyr there are no rows, and MAX of nothing is NULL.

steps.title: Each player's favourite purchase
prompt: For every player who bought something, return **handle**, **item** and **gems** for their **most expensive** purchase. Use a correlated subquery (ties would all be shown; there are none here).
Tables: `players(id, handle, country, joined)` and `purchases(id, player_id, item, gems, day)`.
solution: JOIN purchases AS x ON x.player_id = p.id
WHERE x.gems = (SELECT MAX(y.gems) FROM purchases AS y WHERE y.player_id = p.id);
setup: PRAGMA foreign_keys = ON;
CREATE TABLE players (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, handle TEXT, country TEXT, joined TEXT);
CREATE TABLE purchases (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, player_id INTEGER REFERENCES players(id), item TEXT, gems INTEGER, day TEXT);
hints: Join players to purchases, then keep the purchase whose gems equals that player's MAX.
The MAX comes from a correlated subquery on `y.player_id = p.id`.

steps.title: Big-ticket teams
prompt: Return every **team** (once) that has **at least one** employee earning over **120000** and **no one** earning under **70000**.
Tables: `employees(id, name, title, team, manager_id, salary)`; `manager_id` points at another employee (NULL for the CEO).
solution: WHERE EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM employees AS x WHERE x.team = e.team AND x.salary > 120000)
AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM employees AS x WHERE x.team = e.team AND x.salary < 70000);
setup: PRAGMA foreign_keys = ON;
CREATE TABLE employees (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, name TEXT, title TEXT, team TEXT, manager_id INTEGER REFERENCES employees(id), salary INTEGER);
